$$5(ax-b)=-\frac{(45)}{9}x+\frac{(54)}{(23)}$$

In the given equation, $a$ and $b$ are constants and $b>0$. The equation has no solution. What is the value of $a$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. Distributing $5$ on the left side yields $5ax-5b=-\frac{45}{9}x+\frac{54}{23}$. Simplifying the right side gives $5ax-5b=-5x+\frac{54}{23}$. For a linear equation to have no solution, the coefficients of $x$ on both sides must be equal while the constant terms are not equal. Setting the coefficients of $x$ equal gives $5a=-5$. Dividing both sides by $5$ yields $a=-1$.
